as_told.title: Carter holds the Grill Flame file; Harley Trent's 'road' was a river

plain: The story goes that in the 1970s a psychic spy found a downed Tu-22 aircraft somewhere in Zaire, and that President Jimmy Carter later called it the strangest thing of his presidency. The psychic was a woman named Rosemary Smith, a remote viewer, meaning someone trained to try to see distant places with the mind alone. Michels tells it himself, without naming a source, in two episodes. In one he says Carter went on record in 1976 calling it "the craziest thing I ever experienced in my presidency". In the other he adds that Smith was handed "all of Africa" as her target. A second teller, a man named Joe McMoneagle, passes on what he says Carter told him, and he calls the program's papers "our file". He says Carter held that file in his arm as he spoke: "a green file with a red stripe" marked Grill Flame, the name he gives the government's psychic spying program. McMoneagle also says a man named Harley Trent described a "road" during the search that turned out to be a river. If true, a president would have seen a psychic find a lost plane that ordinary searches could not.
